verses_en.text: There shone Srivasa, an intoxicated bee sporting at Hari's lotus feet: wet with the tears of love, his arms flung up<sup>*</sup>, ever eager, he sings of the Lord in the rapture of the highest rasa. There too was Gopinatha<sup>*</sup>, foremost of the twice-born: as soon as the name of Krishna reached his ears, he would weep aloud again and again in his intoxication and dance beyond all measure, his hands quivering to the rhythm.
verses_en.orig:
श्रीवासो यत्र रेजे हरिपदकमलप्रोल्लसन्मत्तभृङ्गः
प्रेमार्द्रोद्धूतबाहुः परमरसमदैर्गायतीशं सदोत्कः।
गोपीनाथो द्विजाग्र्यः श्रवणपथगते नाम्नि कृष्णस्य मत्तो-
ऽत्युच्चै रौति स्म भूयो लयतरलकरो नृत्यति स्मातिवेलम्॥१९॥
verses_en.translit:
śrīvāso yatra reje haripadakamalaprollasanmattabhṛṅgaḥ
premārdroddhūtabāhuḥ paramarasamadairgāyatīśaṁ sadotkaḥ|
gopīnātho dvijāgryaḥ śravaṇapathagate nāmni kṛṣṇasya matto-
'tyuccai rauti sma bhūyo layataralakaro nṛtyati smātivelam||19||
verses_en.wbw: shrivasah — Srivasa; yatra — where; reje — shone; hari-pada-kamala-prollasan-matta-bhringah — an intoxicated bee sporting at Hari's lotus feet; prema-ardra-uddhuta-bahuh — moist with love, with arms flung up; parama-rasa-madaih — in the rapture of the highest rasa; gayati — sings; isham — the Lord; sada-utkah — ever eager; gopinathah — Gopinatha; dvija-agryah — foremost of the twice-born; shravana-patha-gate — having reached the path of hearing; namni — the name; krishnasya — of Krishna; mattah — intoxicated; ati-uchchaih — very loudly; rauti sma — cried; bhuyah — again; laya-tarala-karah — his hands quivering in rhythm; nrityati sma — danced; ati-velam — beyond measure.
notes: The beginning of the second line of this verse is damaged in the sources; "his arms flung up" is a tentative reading restored by the metre.
Gopinatha is a brahmana of Navadvipa; apparently Gopinatha Acharya, who later appears in Nilachala.

verses_en.text: There shone the lord Sri Advaita, the most excellent, the great soul. Radiant as the rising morning sun, He knew how to awaken the wise as the sun awakens lotuses; like the moon born of the ocean of compassion, He was the one embodiment of the peace that cools the burning in people's hearts. Unsurpassed in loving meditation, rich in the fine gift of the art of dance, He was a teacher of the art of the highest rasa.
verses_en.orig:
बालोद्यद्भास्कराभो बुधजनकमलोद्बोधने दक्षमूर्तिः
कारुण्याब्धिहिमांशोरिव जनहृदयोत्तापशान्त्येकमूर्तिः।
प्रेमध्यानातिदक्षो नटनविधिकलासद्गुणाढ्यो महात्मा
श्रीयुक्ताद्वैतवर्यः परमरसकलाचार्य ईशो विरेजे॥२०॥
verses_en.translit:
bālodyadbhāskarābho budhajanakamalodbodhane dakṣamūrtiḥ
kāruṇyābdhihimāṁśoriva janahṛdayottāpaśāntyekamūrtiḥ|
premadhyānātidakṣo naṭanavidhikalāsadguṇāḍhyo mahātmā
śrīyuktādvaitavaryaḥ paramarasakalācārya īśo vireje||20||
verses_en.wbw: bala-udyad-bhaskara-abhah — radiant as the rising morning sun; budha-jana-kamala-udbodhane — in awakening the lotuses that are the wise; daksha-murtih — skilful; karunya-abdhi-himamshoh — of the moon of the ocean of compassion; iva — like; jana-hridaya-uttapa-shanti-eka-murtih — the very embodiment of cooling the burning of people's hearts; prema-dhyana-ati-dakshah — supreme in loving meditation; natana-vidhi-kala-sad-guna-adhyah — rich in the fine gift of the art of dance; maha-atma — the great soul; shri-yukta-advaita-varyah — the excellent Sri Advaita; parama-rasa-kala-acharyah — teacher of the art of the highest rasa; ishah — the master; vireje — shone.

verses_en.text: There shone brightly the teacher Chandrashekhara, king of the twice-born<sup>*</sup>, endowed with every virtue: at the name of Krishna the hair of his body stood on end, and he was wet with streaming tears.
verses_en.orig:
यत्र सर्वगुणवानतिरेजे चन्द्रशेखरगुरुर्द्विजराजः।
कृष्णनामकृषिताङ्गरुहः स प्रस्खलन्नयनवारिभिरार्द्रः॥२१॥
verses_en.wbw: yatra — where; sarva-gunavan — endowed with every virtue; ati-reje — shone brightly; chandrashekhara-guruh — the teacher Chandrashekhara; dvija-rajah — king of the twice-born; krishna-nama-krishita-anga-ruhah — the hair of whose body stood on end at the name of Krishna; sah — he; praskhalan-nayana-varibhih — with streaming tears; ardrah — wet.
notes: "King of the twice-born" (dvija-raja) is also a poetic name of the moon — a play on the name Chandrashekhara ("Crowned with the Moon").

verses_en.text: There, when the sage Haridasa dances, the Lord of the world, out of love for His servant, at once looks on that dance with delight, together with the hosts of gods who roam the sky, and with Mahesha.
verses_en.orig:
यत्र नृत्यति मुनौ हरिदासे दासवत्सलतया जगदीशः।
खेचरैः सुरगणैः समहेशैर्लास्यमाशु परिपश्यति हृष्टः॥२२॥
verses_en.translit:
yatra nṛtyati munau haridāse dāsavatsalatayā jagadīśaḥ|
khecaraiḥ suragaṇaiḥ samaheśairlāsyamāśu paripaśyati hṛṣṭaḥ||22||
verses_en.wbw: yatra — where; nrityati — while dancing; munau — the sage; haridase — Haridasa; dasa-vatsalataya — out of love for his servant; jagat-ishah — the Lord of the world; khecharaih — moving in the sky; sura-ganaih — with the hosts of gods; sa-maheshaih — together with Mahesha; lasyam — the dance; ashu — at once; paripashyati — watches; hrishtah — delighted.

verses_en.text: There flows the river born from Vishnu's foot — swift, and brimming with the waters of compassion; vying with the Yamuna, daughter of the Sun, and with the Sarayu, she has received Hari, shining like gold<sup>*</sup>.
verses_en.orig:
यत्र विष्णुपदसम्भवा सरिद्वेगवत्यतितरां करुणार्द्रा।
स्पर्धया रविसुतासरयूणां या दधार कनकोज्ज्वलं हरिम्॥२३॥
verses_en.translit:
yatra viṣṇupadasambhavā saridvegavatyatitarāṁ karuṇārdrā|
spardhayā ravisutāsarayūṇāṁ yā dadhāra kanakojjvalaṁ harim||23||
verses_en.wbw: yatra — where; vishnu-pada-sambhava — born from Vishnu's foot; sarit — the river; vegavati — swift; ati-taram — exceedingly; karuna-ardra — moist with compassion; spardhaya — in rivalry; ravi-suta-sarayunam — with the daughter of the Sun (the Yamuna) and the Sarayu; ya — who; dadhara — bore; kanaka-ujjvalam — shining like gold; harim — Hari.
notes: On the banks of the Yamuna Krishna played, on the banks of the Sarayu (in Ayodhya) Rama; the Ganga at Navadvipa has received Gaura.

verses_en.text: There lived Jagannatha — like the moon risen from the ocean of the twice-born race — a teacher of the Vedas, endowed with all virtues, equal to Brihaspati. His mind purified by the mighty yoga of meditation on Krishna's feet, his heart melting with love, he swiftly waxed like the crescent of the new moon.
verses_en.orig:
जगन्नाथस्तस्मिन् द्विजकुलपयोधीन्दुसदृशो-
ऽभवद्वेदाचार्यः सकलगुणयुक्तो गुरुसमः।
स कृष्णाङ्घ्रिध्यानप्रबलतरयोगेन मनसा
विशुद्धः प्रेमार्द्रो नवशशिकलेवाशु ववृधे॥२४॥
verses_en.translit:
jagannāthastasmin dvijakulapayodhīndusadṛśo-
'bhavadvedācāryaḥ sakalaguṇayukto gurusamaḥ|
sa kṛṣṇāṅghridhyānaprabalatarayogena manasā
viśuddhaḥ premārdro navaśaśikalevāśu vavṛdhe||24||
verses_en.wbw: jagannathah — Jagannatha; tasmin — in it (Navadvipa); dvija-kula-payodhi-indu-sadrishah — like the moon in the ocean of the twice-born race; abhavat — there was; veda-acharyah — a teacher of the Vedas; sakala-guna-yuktah — endowed with all virtues; guru-samah — equal to Guru (Brihaspati); sah — he; krishna-anghri-dhyana-prabala-tara-yogena — by the mighty yoga of meditation on Krishna's feet; manasa — in mind; vishuddhah — purified; prema-ardrah — moist with love; nava-shashi-kala — the crescent of the new moon; iva — like; ashu — swiftly; vavridhe — grew.

karnapura-ckm.title: Слава Навадвипы и Ганги; жители города и Адвайта
karnapura-ckm.summary: Хвала Навадвипе на берегу Ганги, её брахманам, врачам и вайшьям; город украшает Адвайта, чья любовь привела Господа.

verses.text: Счастлива эта земля: чистотой своих качеств она выше неба, выше всего небесного. Она привыкла носить великие драгоценности — и потому понесла на себе Навадвипу, драгоценность редчайшую.
verses.orig:
इयं मही भाग्यवती महीयसी
दिवोऽपि दिव्यादपि निर्मलैर्गुणैः ।
महान्ति रत्नानि यदा दधात्यतो
दधौ नवद्वीपमतीव दुर्लभम् ॥१॥
verses.translit:
iyaṁ mahī bhāgyavatī mahīyasī
divo 'pi divyād api nirmalair guṇaiḥ |
mahānti ratnāni yadā dadhāty ato
dadhau navadvīpam atīva durlabham ||1||
verses.wbw: iyam — эта; mahī — земля; bhāgyavatī — счастливая; mahīyasī — величайшая; divaḥ — неба; api — даже; divyāt — небесного [мира]; api — даже; nirmalaiḥ — чистыми; guṇaiḥ — качествами; mahānti — великие; ratnāni — драгоценности; yadā — коль скоро; dadhāti — носит; ataḥ — потому; dadhau — понесла; navadvīpam — Навадвипу; atīva — крайне; durlabham — редкую.

verses.text: Не потому ли так прославилось имя «Навадвипа», что земля, полная нетерпения, собрала отовсюду в одно место всё счастье, копившееся многими путями? И деревья на ней — словно волоски, вставшие дыбом от восторга.
verses.orig:
अनेकधा सञ्चितभाग्यसञ्चयं
समस्तमेकत्र विधाय सर्वतः ।
महीरुहैरुत्पुलकेयमुत्सुका
दधौ नवद्वीप इति प्रथां किमु ॥२॥
verses.translit:
anekadhā sañcita-bhāgya-sañcayaṁ
samastam ekatra vidhāya sarvataḥ |
mahīruhair utpulakeyam utsukā
dadhau navadvīpa iti prathāṁ kimu ||2||
verses.wbw: anekadhā — многообразно; sañcita — накопленного; bhāgya — счастья; sañcayam — запас; samastam — весь; ekatra — в одно место; vidhāya — сложив; sarvataḥ — отовсюду; mahīruhaiḥ — деревьями; utpulakā — с поднявшимися волосками; iyam — она; utsukā — нетерпеливая; dadhau — приняла; navadvīpaḥ — «Навадвипа»; iti — так; prathām — славу, имя; kimu — не… ли.
notes: Mahīruha — «растущее из земли», дерево. Деревья как пулака (волоски, встающие дыбом от экстаза) на теле Земли — классический образ санскритской поэзии.

verses.text: «Когда же нисойдёт Господь?» — думала она, расцветая сердцем. И, захваченная этим желанием, снова и снова принимала на себя следы стоп праведников.
verses.orig:
प्रभुः कदा वावतरिष्यतीत्यदो
विचिन्तयन्त्या मनसि प्रफुल्लया ।
मनोरथाक्रान्तिवशादनेकशः
सतां पदाब्जानुगतिर्यया दधे ॥३॥
verses.translit:
prabhuḥ kadā vāvatariṣyatīty ado
vicintayantyā manasi praphullayā |
manorathākrānti-vaśād anekaśaḥ
satāṁ padābjānugatir yayā dadhe ||3||
verses.wbw: prabhuḥ — Господь; kadā — когда; vā — же; avatariṣyati — нисойдёт; iti — так; adaḥ — это; vicintayantyā — размышлявшей; manasi — в уме; praphullayā — расцветшей; manoratha — желаний; ākrānti — натиска; vaśāt — силою; anekaśaḥ — многократно; satām — праведных; pada — стоп; abja — лотосов; anugatiḥ — следование; yayā — которой; dadhe — было принято.
notes: Земля ждёт Господа и пока «тренируется» на святых: принимает их шаги как предвкушение Его шагов.

verses.text: Под видом Навадвипы земля вновь понесла на себе словно вторую Матхуру. Кто расскажет о благих делах той, чья душа трепещет от восторга прикосновения стоп Господа?
verses.orig:
इयं नवद्वीपमिषेण मेदिनी
दधार भूयो मथुरामिवापराम् ।
वदेदमुष्याः सुकृतानि को नु वा
प्रभोः पदस्पर्शरसाकुलात्मनः ॥४॥
verses.translit:
iyaṁ navadvīpa-miṣeṇa medinī
dadhāra bhūyo mathurām ivāparām |
vaded amuṣyāḥ sukṛtāni ko nu vā
prabhoḥ pada-sparśa-rasākulātmanaḥ ||4||
verses.wbw: iyam — эта; navadvīpa — Навадвипы; miṣeṇa — под видом; medinī — земля; dadhāra — понесла; bhūyaḥ — вновь; mathurām — Матхуру; iva — словно; aparām — другую; vadet — расскажет; amuṣyāḥ — её; sukṛtāni — благие дела; kaḥ — кто; nu vā — же; prabhoḥ — Господа; pada — стоп; sparśa — прикосновения; rasa — восторгом; ākula — взволнованной; ātmanaḥ — [чья] душа.
notes: Матхура — место рождения Кришны. Навадвипа — «вторая Матхура», место рождения Гауранги.

verses.text: Она омыла склон прекрасных спутанных волос Шивы, где блестит гирлянда черепов, и поймала там рыбку, какой прежде не ловила, — отражение лунного серпа.
verses.orig:
आप्लाव्य या धूर्जटिसज्जटातटीं
कपालमालाच्छटया समन्विताम् ।
शशाङ्कलेखाप्रतिबिम्बरूपिणी-
मलब्धपूर्वां शफरीं समासदत् ॥५॥
verses.wbw: āplāvya — омыв; yā — которая; dhūrjaṭi — Дхурджати; sat — прекрасных; jaṭā — спутанных волос; taṭīm — склон; kapāla — черепов; mālā — гирлянды; chaṭayā — блеском; samanvitām — наделённый; śaśāṅka — луны; lekhā — серпа; pratibimba — отражения; rūpiṇīm — имеющую облик; alabdha — не обретённую; pūrvām — прежде; śapharīm — рыбку-шафари; samāsadat — обрела.
notes: Dhūrjaṭi — «носящий тяжёлые спутанные волосы», имя Шивы. Ганга, падая с неба, проходит через волосы Шивы; серп луны на его голове отражается в её воде и кажется серебристой рыбкой шафари. Подлежащее «она» (Ганга) названо прямо только в стихе 6: стихи 5–8 — одно предложение.

verses.text: Она — очищающая, пленительная струя великого мёда с лотосов стоп Господа. Полная нетерпения, неся чистые воды, она устроила себе обитель здесь, в Навадвипе, обняв её со всех сторон.
verses.orig:
प्रभोः पदाम्भोजयुगस्य पावनी
धारा मनोज्ञा मधुनो महीयसः ।
चकार यत्रास्पदमुत्सुका सती
समन्ततोऽसौ विमलाम्बुवाहिनी ॥६॥
verses.translit:
prabhoḥ padāmbhoja-yugasya pāvanī
dhārā manojñā madhuno mahīyasaḥ |
cakāra yatrāspadam utsukā satī
samantato 'sau vimalāmbu-vāhinī ||6||
verses.wbw: prabhoḥ — Господа; pada — стоп; ambhoja — лотосов; yugasya — пары; pāvanī — очищающая; dhārā — струя; manojñā — пленительная; madhunaḥ — мёда; mahīyasaḥ — великого; cakāra — сделала; yatra — где; āspadam — обитель; utsukā — нетерпеливая; satī — будучи; samantataḥ — со всех сторон; asau — она; vimala — чистые; ambu — воды; vāhinī — несущая.
notes: По пуранам, Ганга вытекает из стопы Вишну. Поэтому её вода — «мёд лотосов Его стоп».

verses.text: Сама вода — и всё же иссушает океан мирского бытия. Бела — и всё же приняла тёмное тело. Течёт по земле — и всё же зовётся небесной рекой. Рассеивает заблуждения — и всё же сама кружит игрой водоворотов.
verses.orig:
द्रवस्वरूपापि भवाब्धिशोषिणी
शुभ्रापि यासीद्धृतकृष्णविग्रहा ।
क्षित्याश्रितापि द्युनदीति विश्रुता
भ्रमापहापि भ्रमिविभ्रमावहा ॥७॥
verses.translit:
drava-svarūpāpi bhavābdhi-śoṣiṇī
śubhrāpi yāsīd dhṛta-kṛṣṇa-vigrahā |
kṣity-āśritāpi dyunadīti viśrutā
bhramāpahāpi bhrami-vibhramāvahā ||7||
verses.wbw: drava — жидкая; svarūpā — по природе; api — хотя; bhava — бытия; abdhi — океан; śoṣiṇī — иссушающая; śubhrā — белая; api — хотя; yā — которая; āsīt — была; dhṛta — принявшая; kṛṣṇa — тёмное; vigrahā — тело; kṣiti — на землю; āśritā — опирающаяся; api — хотя; dyu — небесная; nadī — река; iti — так; viśrutā — прославленная; bhrama — заблуждение; apahā — устраняющая; api — хотя; bhrami — водоворотов; vibhrama — игру; āvahā — несущая.
notes: Приём вирóдхабхаса — «мнимое противоречие», каждое разрешается двойным смыслом. Kṛṣṇa-vigraha — «тёмное тело», но и «тело Кришны»: Ганга исходит из стопы Вишну. Bhrama — «заблуждение», bhrami — «кружение, водоворот».

verses.text: И вот она поселилась у края Навадвипы, словно затем, чтобы придать этой земле величайшую красоту. Желая вдохнуть аромат лотосов стоп Господа, она вся взволновалась волнами томления.
verses.orig:
सेयं नवद्वीपभुवो महीयसीं
शोभामिवाधाय तदन्तवासिनी ।
प्रभोः पदाम्भोजयुगस्य सौरभ-
प्राप्त्यै बभूवोत्कलिकाकुलीकृता ॥८॥
(चतुर्भिः कलापकम्)
verses.translit:
seyaṁ navadvīpa-bhuvo mahīyasīṁ
śobhām ivādhāya tad-anta-vāsinī |
prabhoḥ padāmbhoja-yugasya saurabha-
prāptyai babhūvotkalikākulīkṛtā ||8||
verses.wbw: sā — та; iyam — эта; navadvīpa — Навадвипы; bhuvaḥ — земле; mahīyasīm — величайшую; śobhām — красоту; iva — словно; ādhāya — придав; tat — её; anta — у края; vāsinī — живущая; prabhoḥ — Господа; pada — стоп; ambhoja — лотосов; yugasya — пары; saurabha — аромата; prāptyai — для обретения; babhūva — стала; utkalikā — волнами (томлением); ākulī-kṛtā — взволнованной.
notes: В издании слитно «शोभामिवाधायत दन्तवासिनी», что бессмысленно. Делим: iva ādhāya tad-anta-vāsinī — «словно придав…, живущая у её края». Так подтверждает хинди-перевод: «течёт у края Навадвипы». Игра слов: utkalikā — и «волна», и «томление, тоска». Caturbhiḥ kalāpakam — «калапака из четырёх [стихов]».

verses.text: Там живут лучшие из брахманов — «богов на земле». Они всегда верны праведному укладу, отдали себя Высшему, без устали совершают обряды, предписанные Ведами, — словно сами предписания шрути и смрити, принявшие тело.
verses.orig:
वसन्ति यत्र क्षितिदेवसत्तमाः
सदा सदाचारपराः परायणाः ।
निरन्तरं वेदविधानकर्म्मसु
श्रुतिस्मृतीनां विधयः शरीरिणः ॥९॥
verses.translit:
vasanti yatra kṣiti-deva-sattamāḥ
sadā sad-ācāra-parāḥ parāyaṇāḥ |
nirantaraṁ veda-vidhāna-karmasu
śruti-smṛtīnāṁ vidhayaḥ śarīriṇaḥ ||9||
verses.wbw: vasanti — живут; yatra — где; kṣiti — земли; deva — боги; sattamāḥ — лучшие; sadā — всегда; sat — благому; ācāra — поведению; parāḥ — преданные; parāyaṇāḥ — Высшему предавшиеся; nirantaram — непрестанно; veda — Ведами; vidhāna — предписанных; karmasu — в обрядах; śruti — шрути; smṛtīnām — и смрити; vidhayaḥ — предписания; śarīriṇaḥ — воплощённые.
notes: Kṣiti-deva («бог земли») — традиционное именование брахмана.

verses.text: Там живут величайшие из искусных врачей, лучшие из вайшьев, верные своей дхарме, и другие люди — все окружены непревзойдённой, светлой славой.
verses.orig:
प्रभावभाजां भिषजां महत्तमाः
स्वधर्म्मनिष्ठाश्च विशां वराः परे ।
प्रतिष्ठया निःसहशुभ्रया सदा
समन्विता यत्र वसन्ति मानवाः ॥१०॥
verses.translit:
prabhāva-bhājāṁ bhiṣajāṁ mahattamāḥ
sva-dharma-niṣṭhāś ca viśāṁ varāḥ pare |
pratiṣṭhayā niḥsaha-śubhrayā sadā
samanvitā yatra vasanti mānavāḥ ||10||
verses.wbw: prabhāva — силой; bhājām — наделённых; bhiṣajām — врачей; mahattamāḥ — величайшие; sva — своей; dharma — дхарме; niṣṭhāḥ — верные; ca — и; viśām — вайшьев; varāḥ — лучшие; pare — другие; pratiṣṭhayā — славой; niḥsaha — непревзойдённой; śubhrayā — светлой; sadā — всегда; samanvitāḥ — наделённые; yatra — где; vasanti — живут; mānavāḥ — люди.
notes: Niḥsaha — «неодолимый, непревзойдённый»: так в обоих изданиях (и у Госвами, GGM), поэтому прежняя конъектура niḥsama («несравненный», ср. «peerless» у Кушакратхи) не нужна. Bhiṣaj — врачи, каста вайдья; к ней принадлежали Мурари Гупта и сам Кави Карнапура.

verses_en.text: This earth is fortunate: by the purity of her qualities she is greater than heaven, greater even than all that is heavenly. Since she is wont to bear great jewels, she therefore bore Navadvipa, a jewel exceedingly rare.
verses_en.orig:
इयं मही भाग्यवती महीयसी
दिवोऽपि दिव्यादपि निर्मलैर्गुणैः ।
महान्ति रत्नानि यदा दधात्यतो
दधौ नवद्वीपमतीव दुर्लभम् ॥१॥
verses_en.translit:
iyaṁ mahī bhāgyavatī mahīyasī
divo 'pi divyād api nirmalair guṇaiḥ |
mahānti ratnāni yadā dadhāty ato
dadhau navadvīpam atīva durlabham ||1||
verses_en.wbw: iyam — this; mahī — earth; bhāgyavatī — fortunate; mahīyasī — greatest; divaḥ — than heaven; api — even; divyāt — than the heavenly [world]; api — even; nirmalaiḥ — by pure; guṇaiḥ — by qualities; mahānti — great; ratnāni — jewels; yadā — since; dadhāti — bears; ataḥ — therefore; dadhau — bore; navadvīpam — Navadvipa; atīva — exceedingly; durlabham — rare.

verses_en.text: Was it not because this eager earth, her hair standing on end in the form of trees, gathered from everywhere into one place the whole store of good fortune she had amassed in many ways, that she won the renowned name "Navadvipa"?
verses_en.orig:
अनेकधा सञ्चितभाग्यसञ्चयं
समस्तमेकत्र विधाय सर्वतः ।
महीरुहैरुत्पुलकेयमुत्सुका
दधौ नवद्वीप इति प्रथां किमु ॥२॥
verses_en.translit:
anekadhā sañcita-bhāgya-sañcayaṁ
samastam ekatra vidhāya sarvataḥ |
mahīruhair utpulakeyam utsukā
dadhau navadvīpa iti prathāṁ kimu ||2||
verses_en.wbw: anekadhā — in many ways; sañcita — of accumulated; bhāgya — of good fortune; sañcayam — the store; samastam — entire; ekatra — in one place; vidhāya — having put; sarvataḥ — from everywhere; mahīruhaiḥ — with trees; utpulakā — with hair standing on end; iyam — she; utsukā — eager; dadhau — took; navadvīpaḥ — "Navadvipa"; iti — thus; prathām — the fame, the name; kimu — was it not…?
notes: Mahīruha, "that which grows from the earth", is a tree. Trees as the pulaka (the hairs that stand on end in ecstasy) on the body of the Earth are a classical image of Sanskrit poetry.

verses_en.text: "When indeed will the Lord descend?" — so she pondered, blossoming in her heart; and, carried away by the force of this longing, again and again she bore the tread of the lotus feet of the saintly.
verses_en.orig:
प्रभुः कदा वावतरिष्यतीत्यदो
विचिन्तयन्त्या मनसि प्रफुल्लया ।
मनोरथाक्रान्तिवशादनेकशः
सतां पदाब्जानुगतिर्यया दधे ॥३॥
verses_en.translit:
prabhuḥ kadā vāvatariṣyatīty ado
vicintayantyā manasi praphullayā |
manorathākrānti-vaśād anekaśaḥ
satāṁ padābjānugatir yayā dadhe ||3||
verses_en.wbw: prabhuḥ — the Lord; kadā — when; vā — indeed; avatariṣyati — will descend; iti — thus; adaḥ — this; vicintayantyā — by her who was pondering; manasi — in the mind; praphullayā — by her who was blossoming; manoratha — of desire; ākrānti — of the onset; vaśāt — by the force; anekaśaḥ — many times; satām — of the saintly; pada — of the feet; abja — of the lotuses; anugatiḥ — the following (the tread); yayā — by whom; dadhe — was borne.
notes: The earth, awaiting the Lord, "practises" on the saints in the meantime: she receives their steps as a foretaste of His.

verses_en.text: In the guise of Navadvipa this earth bore once again, as it were, a second Mathura. Who indeed could tell the pious deeds of her whose soul is overwhelmed with the delight of the touch of the Lord's feet?
verses_en.orig:
इयं नवद्वीपमिषेण मेदिनी
दधार भूयो मथुरामिवापराम् ।
वदेदमुष्याः सुकृतानि को नु वा
प्रभोः पदस्पर्शरसाकुलात्मनः ॥४॥
verses_en.translit:
iyaṁ navadvīpa-miṣeṇa medinī
dadhāra bhūyo mathurām ivāparām |
vaded amuṣyāḥ sukṛtāni ko nu vā
prabhoḥ pada-sparśa-rasākulātmanaḥ ||4||
verses_en.wbw: iyam — this; navadvīpa — of Navadvipa; miṣeṇa — in the guise; medinī — earth; dadhāra — bore; bhūyaḥ — again; mathurām — Mathura; iva — as if; aparām — another; vadet — could tell; amuṣyāḥ — of her; sukṛtāni — the pious deeds; kaḥ — who; nu vā — indeed; prabhoḥ — of the Lord; pada — of the feet; sparśa — of the touch; rasa — with the delight; ākula — overwhelmed; ātmanaḥ — [of her] whose soul.
notes: Mathura is the birthplace of Krishna; Navadvipa, the birthplace of Gauranga, is a "second Mathura".

verses_en.text: She bathed the slope of Shiva's beautiful matted locks, where the garland of skulls gleams, and there caught a little shaphari fish such as she had never caught before — the reflection of the crescent moon.
verses_en.orig:
आप्लाव्य या धूर्जटिसज्जटातटीं
कपालमालाच्छटया समन्विताम् ।
शशाङ्कलेखाप्रतिबिम्बरूपिणी-
मलब्धपूर्वां शफरीं समासदत् ॥५॥
verses_en.wbw: āplāvya — having bathed; yā — who; dhūrjaṭi — of Dhurjati; sat — of the beautiful; jaṭā — of the matted locks; taṭīm — the slope; kapāla — of skulls; mālā — of the garland; chaṭayā — with the gleam; samanvitām — endowed; śaśāṅka — of the moon; lekhā — of the crescent; pratibimba — of the reflection; rūpiṇīm — having the form; alabdha — not obtained; pūrvām — before; śapharīm — a śapharī fish; samāsadat — obtained.
notes: Dhūrjaṭi, "he who wears heavy matted locks", is a name of Shiva. The Ganga, falling from heaven, passes through Shiva's hair; the crescent moon on his head is reflected in her water and looks like a silvery śapharī fish. The subject, "she" (the Ganga), is named outright only in verse 6: verses 5–8 are one sentence.

verses_en.text: She is the purifying, charming stream of the great honey of the Lord's two lotus feet; and here [in Navadvipa], full of eagerness and carrying pure waters, she made her abode, [embracing it] on all sides.
verses_en.orig:
प्रभोः पदाम्भोजयुगस्य पावनी
धारा मनोज्ञा मधुनो महीयसः ।
चकार यत्रास्पदमुत्सुका सती
समन्ततोऽसौ विमलाम्बुवाहिनी ॥६॥
verses_en.translit:
prabhoḥ padāmbhoja-yugasya pāvanī
dhārā manojñā madhuno mahīyasaḥ |
cakāra yatrāspadam utsukā satī
samantato 'sau vimalāmbu-vāhinī ||6||
verses_en.wbw: prabhoḥ — of the Lord; pada — of the feet; ambhoja — of the lotuses; yugasya — of the pair; pāvanī — purifying; dhārā — stream; manojñā — charming; madhunaḥ — of honey; mahīyasaḥ — of great; cakāra — made; yatra — where; āspadam — an abode; utsukā — eager; satī — being; samantataḥ — on all sides; asau — she; vimala — pure; ambu — waters; vāhinī — carrying.
notes: According to the Puranas, the Ganga flows from the foot of Vishnu; therefore her water is "the honey of His lotus feet".

verses_en.text: Though liquid by nature, she dries up the ocean of worldly existence; though white, she has assumed a dark body; though resting on the earth, she is famed as the heavenly river; though she dispels delusion, she brings the whirling play of eddies.
verses_en.orig:
द्रवस्वरूपापि भवाब्धिशोषिणी
शुभ्रापि यासीद्धृतकृष्णविग्रहा ।
क्षित्याश्रितापि द्युनदीति विश्रुता
भ्रमापहापि भ्रमिविभ्रमावहा ॥७॥
verses_en.translit:
drava-svarūpāpi bhavābdhi-śoṣiṇī
śubhrāpi yāsīd dhṛta-kṛṣṇa-vigrahā |
kṣity-āśritāpi dyunadīti viśrutā
bhramāpahāpi bhrami-vibhramāvahā ||7||
verses_en.wbw: drava — liquid; svarūpā — by nature; api — though; bhava — of worldly existence; abdhi — the ocean; śoṣiṇī — drying up; śubhrā — white; api — though; yā — who; āsīt — was; dhṛta — having assumed; kṛṣṇa — a dark; vigrahā — body; kṣiti — on the earth; āśritā — resting; api — though; dyu — heavenly; nadī — river; iti — thus; viśrutā — famed; bhrama — delusion; apahā — removing; api — though; bhrami — of whirlpools; vibhrama — the play; āvahā — bringing.
notes: The figure of virodhābhāsa, "apparent contradiction": each is resolved by a double meaning. Kṛṣṇa-vigraha is "a dark body", but also "the body of Krishna": the Ganga issues from the foot of Vishnu. Bhrama is "delusion", bhrami "whirling, an eddy".

verses_en.text: And she, dwelling at the edge of Navadvipa as if to impart the greatest beauty to that land, became all astir with waves of longing to obtain the fragrance of the Lord's two lotus feet.
verses_en.orig:
सेयं नवद्वीपभुवो महीयसीं
शोभामिवाधाय तदन्तवासिनी ।
प्रभोः पदाम्भोजयुगस्य सौरभ-
प्राप्त्यै बभूवोत्कलिकाकुलीकृता ॥८॥
(चतुर्भिः कलापकम्)
verses_en.translit:
seyaṁ navadvīpa-bhuvo mahīyasīṁ
śobhām ivādhāya tad-anta-vāsinī |
prabhoḥ padāmbhoja-yugasya saurabha-
prāptyai babhūvotkalikākulīkṛtā ||8||
verses_en.wbw: sā — she; iyam — this; navadvīpa — of Navadvipa; bhuvaḥ — to the land; mahīyasīm — the greatest; śobhām — beauty; iva — as if; ādhāya — having imparted; tat — of it; anta — at the edge; vāsinī — dwelling; prabhoḥ — of the Lord; pada — of the feet; ambhoja — of the lotuses; yugasya — of the pair; saurabha — of the fragrance; prāptyai — for the obtaining; babhūva — became; utkalikā — with waves (with longing); ākulī-kṛtā — agitated.
notes: The edition prints «शोभामिवाधायत दन्तवासिनी», which makes no sense. We divide: iva ādhāya tad-anta-vāsinī, "as if imparting…, dwelling at its edge". A play on words: utkalikā is both "wave" and "longing". Caturbhiḥ kalāpakam — "a kalāpaka of four [verses]".

verses_en.text: There live the best of the brahmanas, the "gods on earth". Ever devoted to righteous conduct, given over to the Supreme, unceasingly [engaged] in the rites enjoined by the Vedas, they are the injunctions of shruti and smriti in bodily form.
verses_en.orig:
वसन्ति यत्र क्षितिदेवसत्तमाः
सदा सदाचारपराः परायणाः ।
निरन्तरं वेदविधानकर्म्मसु
श्रुतिस्मृतीनां विधयः शरीरिणः ॥९॥
verses_en.translit:
vasanti yatra kṣiti-deva-sattamāḥ
sadā sad-ācāra-parāḥ parāyaṇāḥ |
nirantaraṁ veda-vidhāna-karmasu
śruti-smṛtīnāṁ vidhayaḥ śarīriṇaḥ ||9||
verses_en.wbw: vasanti — live; yatra — where; kṣiti — of the earth; deva — gods; sattamāḥ — the best; sadā — always; sat — to good; ācāra — conduct; parāḥ — devoted; parāyaṇāḥ — given over to the Supreme; nirantaram — unceasingly; veda — by the Vedas; vidhāna — enjoined; karmasu — in rites; śruti — of shruti; smṛtīnām — and of smriti; vidhayaḥ — the injunctions; śarīriṇaḥ — embodied.
notes: Kṣiti-deva ("god of the earth") is a traditional designation of a brahmana.

verses_en.text: There live the greatest of able physicians, the best of the vaishyas, faithful to their own dharma, and other people too — all ever endowed with bright, unsurpassed renown.
verses_en.orig:
प्रभावभाजां भिषजां महत्तमाः
स्वधर्म्मनिष्ठाश्च विशां वराः परे ।
प्रतिष्ठया निःसहशुभ्रया सदा
समन्विता यत्र वसन्ति मानवाः ॥१०॥
verses_en.translit:
prabhāva-bhājāṁ bhiṣajāṁ mahattamāḥ
sva-dharma-niṣṭhāś ca viśāṁ varāḥ pare |
pratiṣṭhayā niḥsaha-śubhrayā sadā
samanvitā yatra vasanti mānavāḥ ||10||
verses_en.wbw: prabhāva — power; bhājām — of those possessing; bhiṣajām — of physicians; mahattamāḥ — the greatest; sva — to their own; dharma — dharma; niṣṭhāḥ — faithful; ca — and; viśām — of the vaishyas; varāḥ — the best; pare — others; pratiṣṭhayā — with renown; niḥsaha — unsurpassed; śubhrayā — with bright; sadā — always; samanvitāḥ — endowed; yatra — where; vasanti — live; mānavāḥ — people.
notes: Niḥsaha, "irresistible, unsurpassed": so in both editions (Goswami's, GGM, included), so no conjecture is needed. Bhiṣaj — physicians, the vaidya caste, to which Murari Gupta and Kavi Karnapura himself belonged.

jayananda-cm.ref: Надия-кханда, разд. 3 (фрагм. 3); статья Н. Васу 1897, «Состояние страны»
jayananda-cm.title: Хвала городу Надии: храмы, рынки, боги и гандхарвы в облике брахманов
jayananda-cm.summary: Город Надия на берегу Алакананды подобен Айодхье: храмы, школы, пруды, сады туласи, в каждом доме чтение Веды; боги, риши и гандхарвы родились там брахманами и вайдьями; перечислены утварь, украшения и ткани в доме Мишры и на рынках Надии.

verses.text:
Город, дивный множеством росписей и красок,
в нём живут люди многих каст;
храмы и святилища, обмазанные известью,
деревья и лианы всех цветов.

Слава, слава благословенному городу Надии
на берегу Алакананды!
Камала, прекрасная, играет там,
украшенная гирляндами бакулы.

На каждом доме — дивный навершный сосуд,
трепещут флаги;
как был некогда город Айодхья, —
сверкают, словно вспышки молний.

Залы для плясок, школы, длинные пруды, озёра,
колодцы, водоёмы со ступенями;
обители, павильоны, хорошо устроенные дворы,
сады жасмина-кунды и туласи.

У каждой двери сияют расписные створки,
в каждом переулке — торг;
в каждом переулке радостные пляски и песни,
в каждом доме — чтение Веды.

Приняв облик дваждырождённых, боги и гандхарвы
родились в Навадвипе;
став жёнами брахманов, видьядхари Индры
поют у Ганги.

Покинув небо, все сонмы гандхарвов
родились вайдьями и их жёнами*;
боги, риши и муни, приняв облик брахманов,
изучают шрути и Гиту.
notes: «জন্মিল বৈদ্য বনিতা» — можно понять и как «родились вайдьями и женщинами».

verses.text:
В час, когда пыль поднимается от стад, там мриданги и опахала,
блистают навесы […];
дворы, обнесённые кирпичными стенами,
хорошо устроенные двери домов*.
notes: Строфа дефектна: обе её половины кончаются двойной дандой, части строк, по-видимому, утрачены или переставлены. «Час пыли от стад» (годхули) — сумерки.

verses.text:
Стекло и щиты, расписанные киноварью и аурипигментом,
четырёхстенные беседки, четырёхугольные залы;
в залах — красивые массивные столбы,
украшенные узорами луны и солнца.

Павлины, попугаи, журавли, голуби,
опахала в виде львов и лебедей;
дивные мухогонки-чамары, навесы,
в каждом доме — красивые раковинные браслеты*.
notes: «শাখা» — браслеты из раковины, которые носят замужние женщины; слово может значить и «ветви».

verses.text:
Тазы, шкатулки для бетеля, ларцы для ареки,
зеркала, чашечки для снадобий*;
медные горшки, латунные кувшины для соков,
треножники из Варанаси.
notes: «রসবাটিকা» — букв. «чашечка для соков (снадобий)»; точное значение неясно. «ডাবর» — таз, сосуд для воды.

verses.text:
Шкатулки с отделкой из раковин, блюда-саранги,
плошки, полные сладостей;
[…] кувшины с носиком, медные […],
прохладные латунные кувшины*.
notes: «তিরোহিত» и «মুখারস মন্ডল» не поддаются уверенному толкованию и опущены; «সরঙ্গি» (вид блюда) оставлено как название.

verses.text:
Каменная посуда тонкой работы,
палочки мела и краски*;
ориссийские и гаудийские замки и гребни,
дивные коробочки.
notes: «খড়িকা রঙ্গিকা পড়া» — смысл предположительный; «শাঁপুড়া», переданное как «коробочки», также неясно.

verses.text:
Браслеты-тар, низки раковин-каури, золотые амулеты,
наплечья, запястья, самоцветные ножные браслеты;
золотые украшения в виде листьев кетаки, кораллы, жемчуг,
[изделия] из страны Кашмир*.
notes: «গাঁঠ্যা কড়ি» понято как «нанизанные каури»; «কিআ পাতা» — как украшения в виде листьев кетаки; «খুরে» в последней строке неясно.

verses.text:
Сусальное золото, […] бетель, […],
дивные косы-бени из страны Канчи;
шелка, тонкие ткани, тибетские ткани, сукно-саклат, одеяла,
ткани шрирам-кхани и джамакха;
сапфиры из Тибета,
ткани «лакшми-виласа» и «тарака»*.
notes: Перечень тканей и украшений; многие слова («তবক বসর পান কাটা», «শ্রীরাম খানি», «জমখা», «তারকা») неясны и переданы условно или опущены. «Лакшми-виласа» и «кришна-кели» (см. фрагменты 10 и 11) — названия дорогих тканей.

verses.text:
Не могу описать, сколько слуг и служанок
трудится в доме Мишры;
всё, что редко во всех мирах,
продаётся на рынке Надии.
Размышляя о медовом нектаре стоп-лотосов

Рага сухи.
> Город, дивный множеством росписей и красок,
в нём живут люди многих каст;
храмы и святилища, обмазанные известью,
деревья и лианы всех цветов.
> Слава, слава благословенному городу Надии
на берегу Алакананды!
Камала, прекрасная, играет там,
украшенная гирляндами бакулы.
> На каждом доме — дивный навершный сосуд,
трепещут флаги;
как был некогда город Айодхья, —
сверкают, словно вспышки молний.
> Залы для плясок, школы, длинные пруды, озёра,
колодцы, водоёмы со ступенями;
обители, павильоны, хорошо устроенные дворы,
сады жасмина-кунды и туласи.
> У каждой двери сияют
дивные расписные створки;
в каждом переулке радостные пляски и песни,
в каждом доме — чтение Веды.
> Приняв облик дваждырождённых, боги и гандхарвы
родились в Навадвипе;
став жёнами брахманов, видьядхари Индры
поют у Ганги.
> Покинув небо, все сонмы гандхарвов
родились вайдьями и их жёнами;
боги, риши и муни, приняв облик брахманов,
изучают шрути и Гиту.
> [с. 205]
> В час, когда пыль поднимается от стад*, в каждом доме
звуки мриданги, караталов и раковин;
белые чамары, павлиньи опахала,
и над ними красуются навесы.
> Дворы, обнесённые кирпичными стенами,
хорошо устроенные двери домов;
киноварь, аурипигмент, стекло, щиты,
четырёхстенные беседки, залы с резными косяками.
> В залах — красивые массивные столбы,
украшенные узорами луны и солнца;
павлины, попугаи, журавли, голуби,
львы, лебеди, чакраваки.
> Ложа, скамьи, престолы, сиденья,
беседки, павлиньи опахала;
дивные чамары, навесы,
в каждом доме — красивые раковинные браслеты.
> Тазы, шкатулки для бетеля, ларцы для ареки,
зеркала, чашечки для снадобий;
медные горшки, латунные кувшины для соков,
треножники из Варанаси.
> Шкатулки с отделкой из раковин, чаши, блюда,
плошки, полные сладостей;
тирхутские кувшины с носиком, медные […],
прохладные латунные кувшины*.
> Каменная посуда тонкой работы,
ткани, крашенные мелом*;
ориссийские и гаудийские [замки] и гребни,
дивные коробочки*.
> Браслеты-тар, низки каури, золотые амулеты,
наплечья, запястья, самоцветные ножные браслеты;
золотые украшения в виде листьев кетаки, кораллы, жемчуг,
«кхуры» из страны Кашмир.
> Сусальное золото, шкатулки для бетеля,
дивные косы-бени из страны Канчи… *
шелка, тибетские ткани, сукно-саклат, одеяла,
ткани шрирам-кхани и джамакха;
сапфиры из Тибета,
ткани «лакшми-виласа» и «тарака».
> Не могу описать, сколько слуг и служанок
трудится в храме любви*;
всё, что редко во всех мирах,
продаётся на рынке Надии.
> Размышляя о медовом нектаре стоп-лотосов
Чайтаньи и Гададхары, владыки жизни,
поёт брахман Джаянанда «Чайтанья-мангалу»,
сокровенную тайну нигам.
notes: Т. е. в сумерки (годхули). Эта и следующая строфы у Васу полнее, чем в издании 1971 г. (ср. фрагмент 3, строфы 8–10).
«তিরোহুত গাড়ু» — понято как «тирхутские (из Тирхута, Митхилы) кувшины», что подтверждает пересказ Васу ниже («ত্রিহুতের গাড়ু»); «তাম্রমুখার মণ্ডল» не поддаётся толкованию.
«খড়িকা রঙ্গিকা পড়া» — так понимает Васу в пересказе ниже («খড়িকা রঙের কাপড়»).
Слово «замки» (কুলুপ) в OCR цитаты выпало; оно есть в пересказе Васу ниже и в издании 1971 г.
После этой строки у Васу стоят звёздочки — вероятно, знак пропуска.
«প্রেমের মন্দিরে» — так у Васу; в издании 1971 г. здесь «в доме Мишры».

verses_en.text:
A city wondrous with many paintings and colours,
where people of many castes dwell;
temples and shrines plastered with lime,
trees and creepers of every hue.

Glory, glory to the blessed city of Nadia
on the bank of the Alakananda!
Kamala, the lovely, plays there,
adorned with bakula garlands.

On every house a wondrous finial pot,
fluttering banners fly;
as once was the city of Ayodhya —
they flash like strokes of lightning.

Dance-halls, schools, long ponds, lakes,
wells, tanks with flights of steps;
monasteries, pavilions, well-built courtyards,
gardens of kunda jasmine and tulasi.

At every door painted panels shine,
in every lane a market is held;
in every lane joyous dancing and song,
in every house the recitation of the Veda.

Taking the form of the twice-born, gods and gandharvas
were born in Navadvipa;
becoming brahmanas' wives, Indra's vidyadharis
sing beside the Ganga.

Leaving heaven, all the hosts of gandharvas
were born as vaidyas and their wives;*
gods, rishis and munis, taking the form of brahmanas,
study the shruti and the Gita.
notes: "জন্মিল বৈদ্য বনিতা" may also be understood as "were born as vaidyas and as women".

verses_en.text:
At the hour of cow-dust, mridangas and fans there,
canopies gleam […];
courtyards walled with brick,
well-made doors of houses.*
notes: The stanza is defective: both its halves end with a double danda, and parts of lines seem to be lost or displaced. The "hour of cow-dust" (godhuli) is dusk.

verses_en.text:
Glass and shields painted with vermilion and orpiment,
four-walled pavilions, four-sided halls;
in the halls handsome, massive pillars
adorned with marks of moon and sun.

Peacocks, parrots, cranes, doves,
fans shaped as lions and swans;
wondrous yak-tail whisks, canopies,
in every house fine conch-shell bangles.*
notes: "শাখা": bangles of conch-shell, worn by married women; the word can also mean "branches".

verses_en.text:
Basins, betel boxes, areca caskets,
mirrors, little cups for unguents;*
copper pots, brass pitchers for juices,
tripods from Varanasi.
notes: "রসবাটিকা", literally "little cup for juices (unguents)"; the exact sense is unclear. "ডাবর" is a basin or water vessel.

verses_en.text:
Betel boxes inlaid with conch-shell, sarangi platters,
bowls all full of sweets;
[…] spouted water-pots, copper […],
cool brass ewers.*
notes: "তিরোহিত" and "মুখারস মন্ডল" cannot be interpreted with confidence and are omitted; "সরঙ্গি" (a kind of platter) is kept as a name.

verses_en.text:
Stone vessels of fine workmanship,
sticks of chalk and paint;*
Oriya and Gaudiya locks and combs,
wondrous little caskets.
notes: "খড়িকা রঙ্গিকা পড়া": the sense is conjectural; "শাঁপুড়া", given as "little caskets", is also unclear.

verses_en.text:
Tar bracelets, strings of cowries, golden amulets,
armlets, wrist-bangles, jewelled anklets;
gold ornaments shaped like ketaki leaves, coral, pearls,
[wares] from the land of Kashmir.*
notes: "গাঁঠ্যা কড়ি" is taken as "strung cowries", "কিআ পাতা" as ornaments shaped like ketaki leaves; "খুরে" in the last line is unclear.

verses_en.text:
Gold leaf, […] betel, […],
wondrous beni braids from the land of Kanchi;
silks, fine muslins, Tibetan cloth, saklat broadcloth, blankets,
shriram-khani and jamakha fabrics;
sapphires from Tibet,
lakshmi-vilasa and taraka cloths.*
notes: A list of fabrics and ornaments; many words ("তবক বসর পান কাটা", "শ্রীরাম খানি", "জমখা", "তারকা") are unclear and are rendered tentatively or omitted. "Lakshmi-vilasa" and "krishna-keli" (see Fragments 10 and 11) are names of costly fabrics.

verses_en.text:
I cannot write how many servants and maids
toil in Mishra's house;
whatever is rare in all the worlds
is sold in the market of Nadia.
Meditating on the honey of the lotus feet

"In the land of Srihatta lawlessness and famine arose;
dacoity, theft, drought and pestilence set in.
> The land fell into ruin; seeing the calamity,
all the people fled away to various lands.
> Nilambara Chakravarti and Mishra Purandara
with all their kin quickly left Jayapura.
> 'In what land shall we live?' all of them reasoned.
'In this land we shall find no protection; let us go elsewhere.
> A dwelling fit for us all is on the bank of the Ganga,
just as Nanda left Gokula because of its calamities.
> Long ago a king of ascetics told me:
"Leave this land and go into the very midst of Nadia."
> A lawless land is not fit to live in;
in Srihatta not half a sesame seed's worth of good people remains.
> One should live among people whose love and mind are for Krishna,
where there are ascetics purified by the tirthas, full of knowledge, who have conquered the senses,
> where they have faith in the Ganga, the Vaishnavas and mahaprasada —
in people of little fortune these things are not manifest.
> We shall bathe in the Ganga and live in Navadvipa:
that is living in Vaikuntha — what need then of japa and austerity?'
> Riding in fine palanquins, Mishra came with his kin,
and he saw the Ganga and Navadvipa and floated in the bliss of prema.
> Navadvipa is heaven on earth in all the circle of the world;
people of many classes live on the bank of the Jahnavi.
> Meditating on the lotus feet of Chaitanya-chandra,
Jayananda sings the Lord's mangala in bliss.
> Raga Suhi.
> A city wondrous with many paintings and colours,
where people of many castes dwell;
temples and shrines plastered with lime,
trees and creepers of every hue.
> Glory, glory to the blessed city of Nadia
on the bank of the Alakananda!
Kamala, the lovely, plays there,
adorned with bakula garlands.
> On every house a wondrous finial pot,
fluttering banners fly;
as once was the city of Ayodhya —
they flash like strokes of lightning.
> Dance-halls, schools, long ponds, lakes,
wells, tanks with flights of steps;
monasteries, pavilions, well-built courtyards,
gardens of kunda jasmine and tulasi.
> At every door there shine
wondrous painted panels;
in every lane joyous dancing and song,
in every house the recitation of the Veda.
> Taking the form of the twice-born, gods and gandharvas
were born in Navadvipa;
becoming brahmanas' wives, Indra's vidyadharis
sing beside the Ganga.
> Leaving heaven, all the hosts of gandharvas
were born as vaidyas and their wives;
gods, rishis and munis, taking the form of brahmanas,
study the shruti and the Gita.
> [p. 205]
> At the hour of cow-dust,* in every house,
the sound of mridanga, kartal and conch;
white yak-tail whisks, peacock fans,
and canopies gleaming above them.
> Courtyards walled with brick,
well-made doors of houses;
vermilion, orpiment, glass, shields,
four-walled pavilions, halls with carved door-frames.
> In the halls handsome, massive pillars
adorned with marks of moon and sun;
peacocks, parrots, cranes, doves,
lions, swans, chakravakas.
> Bedsteads, benches, thrones, seats,
pavilions, peacock fans;
wondrous yak-tail whisks, canopies,
in every house fine conch-shell bangles.
> Basins, betel boxes, areca caskets,
mirrors, little cups for unguents;
copper pots, brass pitchers for juices,
tripods from Varanasi.
> Boxes inlaid with conch-shell, bowls, platters,
little dishes full of sweets;
spouted water-pots from Tirhut, copper […],
cool brass ewers.*
> Stone vessels of fine workmanship,
cloth dyed with chalk colour;*
Oriya and Gaudiya [locks] and combs,
wondrous little caskets.*
> Tar bracelets, strings of cowries, golden amulets,
armlets, wrist-bangles, jewelled anklets;
gold ornaments shaped like ketaki leaves, coral, pearls,
"khuras" from the land of Kashmir.
> Gold leaf, betel boxes,
wondrous beni braids from the land of Kanchi… *
silks, Tibetan cloth, saklat broadcloth, blankets,
shriram-khani and jamakha fabrics;
sapphires from Tibet,
lakshmi-vilasa and taraka cloths.
> I cannot write how many servants and maids
toil in the temple of love;*
whatever is rare in all the worlds
is sold in the market of Nadia.
> Meditating on the honey of the lotus feet
of Chaitanya and Gadadhara, the lord of his life,
the brahmana Jayananda sings the Chaitanya-mangala,
the deep secret of the nigamas.
> Raga Kanada.
> To Shachi eight daughters were born in due time;
by the bond of fate some time went by.
> Jagannatha Mishra became Mishra Purandara —
a good poet, a pandita, a great logician, handsome.
> Seeing his severe austerity, all people marvelled:
bathing, sandhya, the daily shraddha — the observances of a brahmana;
> offerings, homa, japa, sacrifice, puja with incense and lamps,
reading the Sri Bhagavata before Govinda.
> Another son was born, named Vishvarupa;
a great famine arose in the village of Navadvipa.
> Seeing the calamity — incessant dacoity and theft —
all the people fled away to various lands.
> Then Jagannatha Mishra joyfully
performed Vishvarupa's ten rites one after another.
> Suddenly in Navadvipa there came fear of the king:
seizing brahmanas, the king takes their caste and their life.
> [p. 206]
> In whatever house in Navadvipa he hears the sound of a conch,
he takes its owner's wealth and life and destroys his caste.
> If he sees tilaka on a forehead, a sacred thread on a shoulder,
he loots house and home and binds the man in fetters.
> He breaks temples and shrines, uproots the tulasi;
in fear for their lives the people of Navadvipa have no peace.
> He forbade bathing in the Ganga at all the markets and ghats;
ashvattha and jackfruit trees are cut down by hundreds.
> All the yavanas who lived in the village of Piralya
brought ruin on the brahmanas of Navadvipa.
> Strife between brahmanas and yavanas has gone on from age to age;
the dreadful village of Piralya lies near Navadvipa.
> Before the lord of Gauda they made a false accusation:
'The brahmanas of Navadvipa will bring you calamity.
> There is a prophecy that a brahmana will become king in Gauda;
do not be careless, lest calamity follow.
> A brahmana of Navadvipa will surely become king;
it is written by the gandharvas that his subjects will bear bows.'*
> This lie lodged in the king's mind,
and the king gave the order: 'Lay Nadia waste!'
> Visharada's son, Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya,
went with his whole family to Utkala, leaving the kingdom of Gauda.
> In Utkala the warlike king Prataparudra
honoured Sarvabhauma on a jewelled throne.
> His brother Vidya-vachaspati stayed on in Gauda;
Visharada took up residence in Varanasi.
> Vidya-virinchi and Vidyaranya in Navadvipa,
Bhattacharya-shiromani in the sight of all.
> The lord of Gauda heard that Nadia had been laid waste,
and at night he saw a most terrible dream.
> Kali, bearing sword and skull-cup, naked,
a garland of heads on her neck, crying 'Cut! Cut!' —
> seizing the king by the hair, she drove a spear into his chest
and poured boiling oil into his ears and nostrils:
> 'Today I will throw your capital of Gauda into the Ganga;
I will cut down your whole line, your elephants, horses and troops!'
> The lord of Gauda says: 'Mother, spare my body!
I will resettle Navadvipa, if you save my life!'
> The king rubbed his nose on the ground,* and then Kali let him go;
the lord of Gauda fainted and fell to the earth.
> In the morning he told the dream to his confidant;
hearing of the wondrous dream, all people were seized with dread.
> 'The command of the lord of Gauda: let Navadvipa dwell in happiness;
there is no royal tax — let all people plough their fields.
> Whoever from today obstructs the markets and ghats
shall pay a fine to the treasury and be impaled on the stake.
> Whoever breaks temples and shrines, whoever cuts an ashvattha —
impale him on a stake in the market of Nadia.
> Let all the vaidyas and brahmanas who live in Navadvipa
hold all manner of festivals to their hearts' content.
> Let dance, song and music sound in every house;
let banners fly on the finials above the temples.
> Let there be flower markets, a profusion of perfumes;
let conch, bell and instruments sound with cries of victory.
> As Navadvipa was a capital in former days,
let it be heard of as a hundred times greater.
> If you see a yavana within the bounds of Navadvipa,
kill him at your own will — or spare him.*
> Worship the gods in happiness, perform sacrifice, homa and charity;
the markets and ghats are not forbidden — let them bathe in the Ganga.
> What authority have I over the subjects of Navadvipa?
Truly, truly I say: they are the essence of the world.'
> By the king's command Navadvipa was created anew;
in autumn, at the end of the night, there was a rain of flowers.
> [p. 207]
> The great men who had left the village
all came back to Navadvipa, their wishes fulfilled.
> Meditating on the two feet of Chaitanya and Gadadhara,
Jayananda composes the Nadia-khanda in bliss."
notes: I.e. at dusk (godhuli). This and the following stanza are fuller in Vasu than in the 1971 edition (cf. Fragment 3, stanzas 8–10).
"তিরোহুত গাড়ু" is taken as "water-pots from Tirhut (Mithila)," which Vasu's paraphrase below confirms ("ত্রিহুতের গাড়ু"); "তাম্রমুখার মণ্ডল" cannot be interpreted.
"খড়িকা রঙ্গিকা পড়া" — so understood by Vasu in his paraphrase below ("খড়িকা রঙের কাপড়").
The word "locks" (কুলুপ) has dropped out of the OCR of the quotation; it is present in Vasu's paraphrase below and in the 1971 edition.
After this line Vasu has asterisks, probably marking an omission.
"প্রেমের মন্দিরে" — so in Vasu; the 1971 edition has "in Mishra's house" here.
"গন্ধর্বে লিখন আছে ধনুর্ময় প্রজা" — the sense is unclear; cf. Fragment 4, n. 25.
"নাকে খত দিল," literally "gave a bond with his nose," i.e. humbly owned his fault.
"আপন ইচ্ছায় মার প্রাণ জার রাখ" — the sense is unclear.

cb.title: Харидас: из Будханы в Пхулию; встреча с Адвайтой; экстаз имени
cb.summary: Харидас, олицетворение преданности Вишну, родился в Будхане и поселился в Пхулии близ Шантипура; Адвайта при встрече с ним громко кричит от радости; Харидас странствует по берегам Ганги, громко воспевая имена, танцует, рычит, плачет, смеётся, теряет сознание; ему кланяются даже грешники, а брахманы Пхулии исполнены веры в него.

verses.text:
В это время в Навадвипу пришел Харидас Тхакур. Он был олицетворением преданности Господу Вишну.
эбе ш́уна харида̄са-т̣ха̄курера катха̄
йа̄ха̄ра ш́раван̣е кр̣ш̣н̣а па̄ибе сарватха̄

Теперь услышьте о деяниях Харидаса Тхакура. Слушая о них, вы непременно достигнете Господа Кришны.
буд̣ха̄на-гра̄мете аватӣрн̣а харида̄са
се-бха̄гйе се-саба деш́е кӣртана-прака̄ш́а

Харидас Тхакур родился в деревне Будхан, благодаря чему там и по сей день прославляют Кришну.
ката-дина тха̄кийа̄ а̄ила̄ ган̇га̄-тӣре
а̄сийа̄ рахила̄ пхулийа̄йа ш́а̄нтипурӣ

Некоторое время спустя Харидас перебрался на берег Ганги, в деревню Пхулию, неподалеку от Шантипура.
па̄ийа̄ та̄ха̄на сан̇га а̄ча̄рйа-госа̄н̃и
хун̇ка̄ра карена, а̄нандера анта на̄и

Встретив Харидаса, Адвайта Ачарья был безгранично счастлив. Испытывая духовное блаженство, Он громко закричал.
харида̄са-т̣ха̄кур о адваита-дева-сан̇ге
бха̄сена говинда-раса-самудра-таран̇ге

Общаясь с Адвайтой, Харидас Тхакур также погрузился в волны океана преданности Кришне.
наравадхи харида̄са ган̇га̄-тӣре-тӣре
бхрамен̣а каутуке ‘кр̣ш̣н̣а’ бали’ уччашваре

Харидас постоянно странствовал по берегам Ганги, громко воспевая святые имена Кришны.
виш̣айа-сукхете вирактера аграган̣йа
кр̣ш̣н̣а-на̄ме парипӯрн̣а ш́рӣ-вадана дханйа

Харидас был самым знаменитым из тех, кто отверг наслаждения этого мира. Его уста никогда не покидало Святое Имя Кришны.
кш̣ан̣ека говинда-на̄ме на̄хика виракти
бхакти-расе анукш̣ан̣а хайа на̄на̄ мӯрти

Ни на мгновение у него не ослабевала привязанность к именам Говинды. Поэтому в его теле всегда были заметны признаки трансцендентного экстаза.
какхано карена нр̣тйа а̄пана̄-а̄пани
какхано карена матта-сим̇ха-пра̄йа дхвани

Иногда он забывался в танце, а порой рычал, как разгневанный лев.
какхано ва̄ уччаих̣сваре карена родана
ат̣т̣а-ат̣т̣а маха̄-ха̄сйа ха̄сена какхана

Иногда он громко плакал, а порой безудержно смеялся.
какхано гарджджена ати хун̇ка̄ра карийа̄
какхано мӯрччхита хаи’ тха̄кена пад̣ийа̄

Иногда он громогласно что-то выкрикивал, а порой падал на землю без чувств.
кш̣ан̣е алаукика ш́абда балена да̄кийа̄
кш̣ан̣е та̄и ва̄кха̄нена уттама карийа̄

Иногда из его уст вырывались нечленораздельные звуки, и позже он объяснял окружающим их смысл.
аш́рупа̄та, ромахарш̣а, ха̄сйа, мӯрччха̄, гхарма
кр̣ш̣н̣а-бхакти-вика̄рера йата а̄чхе марма

В нем проявлялись признаки экстатической любви к Кришне: он плакал, смеялся, его тело покрывалось испариной, волосы вставали дыбом, а иногда он терял сознание.
прабху харида̄са ма̄тра нр̣тйе правеш́иле
сакала а̄сийа̄ та̄’на ш́рӣ-виграхе миле

Как только Харидас начинал танцевать, в его теле проявлялись видны все эти признаки.
хена се а̄нанда-дха̄ра̄, тите сарва-ан̇га
ати-па̄ш̣ан̣д̣ӣ о декхи’ па̄йа маха̄-ран̇га

Все тело Харидаса Тхакура становилось мокрым от слез любви. Даже худшие из грешников выражали ему почтение.
киба̄ се адбхута ан̇ге ш́рӣ-пулака̄вали
брахма̄-ш́ива о декхийа̄ хайена кутӯхалӣ

Даже Брахма и Шива приходили в ликование, наблюдая, как волоски на теле Харидаса вставали дыбом от переполняющих его чувств.
пхулийа̄-гра̄мера йата бра̄хман̣а-сакала
сабеи та̄ха̄не декхи’ хаила̄ вихвала

Все брахманы Пхулии, встречая Харидаса, преисполнялись радостью.
саба̄ра та̄ха̄не бад̣а джанмила виш́ва̄са
пхулийа̄йа рахилена прабху-харида̄са

Когда Харидас жил в Пхулии, вера в него крепла в сердце каждого.
ган̇га̄-сна̄на кари’ ниравадхи хари-на̄ма
учча кари’ лаийа̄ булена сарва-стха̄на
Он регулярно совершал омовение в Ганге, а затем бродил по округе, громко призывая имена Господа Хари.

cb.title: Харидас приходит в Навадвипу к Адвайте и вайшнавам
cb.summary: Печалясь о мире, погружённом в чувственность, Харидас приходит в Навадвипу; Адвайта встречает его как самого дорогого друга, вайшнавы любят его; вместе они говорят об оскорблениях безбожников и обсуждают Гиту и «Бхагавату».

verses.text:
Харидас печалился, видя, что весь мир погружен в чувственные наслаждения. Воспевая святые имена Кришны, он глубоко вздыхал.
ката-дине ‘ваиш̣н̣ава’ декхите иччха̄ кари’
а̄илена харида̄са навадвӣпа-пурӣ

Несколько дней спустя Харидас отправился в Навадвипу, чтобы повидаться с живущими там вайшнавами.
харида̄се декхийа̄ сакала бхакта-ган̣а
хаилена атиш́айа пара̄нанда-мана

Все вайшнавы Навадвипы обрадовались, увидев Харидаса.
а̄ча̄рйа-госа̄н̃и харида̄сере па̄ийа̄
ра̄кхилена пра̄н̣а хаите адхика карийа̄

Адвайта Ачарья встретил Харидаса как самого дорогого друга или близкого родственника.
сарва-ваиш̣н̣авера прӣти харида̄са-прати
харида̄с о карена саба̄ре бхакти ати

Все вайшнавы проявляли огромную любовь к Харидасу и были преданы ему, и он отвечал им взаимностью.
па̄ш̣ан̣д̣ӣ-сакале йата дейа ва̄кйа-джва̄ла̄
анйо’нйе сабе та̄ха̄ кахите ла̄гила̄

Собираясь вместе, они обсуждали оскорбительные речи безбожников.
гӣта̄-бха̄гавата лаи’ сарва-бхакта-ган̣а
анйо’нйе вича̄ре тха̄кена сарва-кш̣ан̣а

После этого преданные обсуждали темы «Бхагавад-гиты» и «Шримад-Бхагаватам».
йе-джане пад̣айе ш́унайе э-саба а̄кхйа̄на
та̄ха̄ре милибе гаурачандра бхагава̄н

Тот, кто слушает или читает об этих божественных лилах преданных Господа, обязательно достигнет лотосных стоп Верховной Личности Бога, Шри Гаурачандры.
ш́рӣ кр̣ш̣н̣а-чаитанйа нитйа̄нанда-ча̄нда джа̄на
вр̣нда̄вана да̄са тачху пада-йуге га̄на
Шри Кришна Чайтанья и Шри Нитьянанда – моя жизнь и душа! Так поет славу Их лотосным стопам Вриндаван дас.

advaita-prakasha.title: Харидас уходит в Пхулию: посвящение брахмана Рамдаса; лесная хижина в Бенаполе
advaita-prakasha.summary: С дозволения Адвайты, сказавшего, что кто поклоняется Кришне, тот из касты вайшнавов, Харидас уходит в Пхулию; учёный брахман Рамдас, услышав о превосходстве бхакти над знанием, получает от него Имя; затем, не желая привязываться к месту, Харидас уходит в лес Бенаполя, где селяне строят ему хижину, и он повторяет десять миллионов имён в месяц, служа Туласи.

verses.text: Слава, слава Шри Чайтанье! Слава Ситанатхе! Слава Нитьянанде-Раме вместе с преданными!
Однажды Тхакур Шри Брахма Харидас смиренно поведал Господу желание своего сердца:
«О Господи, позволь мне уйти в уединение, чтобы непрестанно вкушать нектар имени Хари».
Господь ответил: «Разлука с тобой разрывает Мне грудь, но запретить не могу — это стало бы помехой твоему бхаджану».
Харидас простёрся у стоп Господа, а Господь в экстазе любви крепко его обнял.
Харидас сказал: «Я — неприкасаемый грешник. Зачем, коснувшись моего тела, Ты делаешь меня оскорбителем?»
Господь ответил: «Я не понимаю, что такое высокая и низкая каста: кто поклоняется Кришне, тот из касты вайшнавов.
Высоким или низким человека называют по его делам: кто поклоняется Кришне, того Я называю лучшим из всех.
Ты — лучший среди чистых бхагават: от твоего прикосновения в душе прорастает семя преданности».
Харидас сказал: «Господи, всё возможно, если на душу падёт Твоя чистейшая милость».
Сказав так, он, сложив ладони, получил дозволение Господа и, вспоминая Хари, отправился в селение Пхулия.
Все брахманы, жившие в том городе, при виде Харидаса растрогались сердцем.
Был там учёный брахман по имени Рамдас — знаток дхарма-шастр, неизменно преданный дхарме.
Увидев Харидаса, он исполнился преданности и смиренно, ласково заговорил:
«Садху, твоим приходом мы осчастливлены. Не знаю, сколько прежних заслуг было у нашего селения!
От общения с садху дом становится святым. Смилуйся, Господин, поселись здесь».
Брахма Харидас сказал: «О лучший из брахманов, по слову Вед всякий брахман — тело Вишну.
Я низкого рода и не достоин прикосновения. То, что я обрёл общение с тобой, — моя великая удача».
Рамдас сказал: «Садху, к чему такое смирение? У того, кто любит Бога, касту не считают.
Как железо от прикосновения философского камня становится золотом, так в поклонении Богу всякое сословие становится лучшим.
Что хвалить в человеке? Хвалить надо его дхарму: высоким или низким называют по собственным делам.
Кто оставил мирские желания и любит Бога, тот лучший из всех существ и причастен освобождению».
Харидас ответил: «Ты — извечный садху: ты во всех существах видишь садху.
Кто поклоняется Богу путём знания, тот достигает лишь освобождения — по мере силы своего знания.
Мудрый садху не желает освобождения: путём одного знания душа не обретает вечной свободы».
Брахман спросил: «Что же есть, кроме знания, через что достигается Высший Брахман, суть всех сутей?»
Брахма Харидас ответил: «Суть всего — путь преданности: им достигается вечный Брахман, владыка всего.
По природе преданности возникает самосознание слуги, а слуге Хари дарует вечно совершенное тело.
Вечная реальность Брахмана — это Сам Бхагаван, исполненный бытия, сознания и блаженства, всемогущий.
Имя Хари — причина чистой преданности: кто непрестанно повторяет его, обретает вечное сокровище любви.
Когда любовь постепенно сгущается, обретают настроение гопи, а в сладостной расе мадхурьи обретают Радху и Кришну».
Услышав это, брахман весь покрылся мурашками и сказал: «Смилуйся, посвяти меня».
Услышав это, Харидас, исполненный любви, передал брахману силу и дал ему имя Хари.
Обретя величайшее сокровище, брахман залился слезами; он поклонился Харидасу и вознёс ему хвалу.
Постепенно в общении с садху брахман стал вайшнавом, и на ниве его сердца взошла лиана желаний — преданность.
С помощью брахмана Брахма Харидас построил хижину и жил в ней в радости.
Он непрестанно вкушал нектар имени Хари, и все жители селения стали его преданными.
Однажды Харидас задумался: «Нехорошо долго жить на одном месте.
От бесед и общения возникает связь с майей, и мало-помалу душа слепнет от привязанности к миру.
Так не сохранить дхарму отрешённого; поэтому лучше всего оставить общество людей».
Подумав так, он на исходе ночи покинул жилище и, распевая имя Хари, ушёл в Бенаполь.
Там, посреди глухого леса, он пел санкиртану, а люди из селения приходили поклоняться ему.
Того великого счастливца, к кому милостив Кришна, — всякое существо, увидев, исполняется преданности.
Видя сияние, исходящее от тела Брахмы Харидаса, постепенно все жители селения стали его преданными.
В том лесу Бенаполя деревенские преданные заботливо построили ему хижину.
Живя там, садху служил Туласи и за месяц повторял десять миллионов имён.
Он просил подаяние — горсть риса — в домах брахманов-вайшнавов; такова природа милости: учить души праведности.

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
One day Thakura Sri Brahma Haridasa humbly told the Lord the desire of his heart:
"O Lord, allow me to go into solitude, so that I may ceaselessly taste the nectar of the name of Hari."
The Lord replied: "Separation from you breaks My heart, but I cannot forbid it — that would hinder your bhajana."
Haridasa prostrated himself at the Lord's feet, and the Lord in the ecstasy of love embraced him tightly.
Haridasa said: "I am an untouchable sinner. Why do You make me an offender by touching my body?"
The Lord replied: "I do not understand what high or low caste is: whoever worships Krishna is of the caste of Vaishnavas.
A person is called high or low according to his deeds: whoever worships Krishna I call the best of all.
You are the best among pure bhagavatas: by your touch the seed of devotion sprouts in a soul."
Haridasa said: "Lord, everything is possible if Your most pure mercy falls upon a soul."
Having said this, he joined his palms, received the Lord's leave and, remembering Hari, set out for the village of Phuliya.
All the brahmanas living in that town were moved at heart on seeing Haridasa.
There was a learned brahmana there named Ramadasa — versed in the scriptures of dharma, ever devoted to dharma.
Seeing Haridasa, he was filled with devotion and spoke humbly and kindly:
"Sadhu, by your coming we are made fortunate. I do not know how much merit our village had from the past!
By association with a sadhu a house becomes holy. Have mercy, master, and settle here."
Brahma Haridasa said: "O best of brahmanas, according to the Vedas every brahmana is the body of Vishnu.
I am of low birth and not fit to be touched. That I have obtained your company is my great good fortune."
Ramadasa said: "Sadhu, why such humility? For one who loves God, caste is not counted.
As iron becomes gold at the touch of the philosopher's stone, so in the worship of God every class becomes the best.
What is there to praise in a person? One should praise his dharma: high or low one is called by one's own deeds.
Whoever has given up worldly desires and loves God is the best of all beings and has a share in liberation."
Haridasa replied: "You are a sadhu by nature: you see sadhus in all beings.
Whoever worships God by the path of knowledge attains only liberation — according to the power of his knowledge.
The wise sadhu does not desire liberation: by the path of knowledge alone a soul does not obtain eternal freedom."
The brahmana asked: "What is there besides knowledge through which the Supreme Brahman, the essence of essences, is attained?"
Brahma Haridasa replied: "The essence of all is the path of devotion: by it the eternal Brahman, the Lord of all, is attained.
By the nature of devotion the self-conception of a servant arises, and to His servant Hari gives an eternally perfect body.
The eternal reality of Brahman is Bhagavan Himself, full of being, consciousness and bliss, all-powerful.
The name of Hari is the cause of pure devotion: whoever chants it ceaselessly obtains the eternal treasure of love.
When love gradually deepens, one attains the mood of the gopis, and in the sweet rasa of madhurya one attains Radha and Krishna."
Hearing this, the brahmana's hair stood on end all over his body, and he said: "Have mercy, initiate me."
Hearing this, Haridasa, full of love, imparted power to the brahmana and gave him the name of Hari.
Having obtained the greatest treasure, the brahmana shed floods of tears; he bowed to Haridasa and offered him praise.
Gradually, in the company of the sadhu, the brahmana became a Vaishnava, and in the field of his heart the wish-fulfilling creeper of devotion sprang up.
With the brahmana's help Brahma Haridasa built a hut and lived in it joyfully.
He ceaselessly tasted the nectar of the name of Hari, and all the villagers became his devotees.
One day Haridasa reflected: "It is not good to live long in one place.
From conversation and company comes a connection with maya, and little by little the soul is blinded by attachment to the world.
Thus the dharma of the detached is not preserved; therefore it is best to give up the company of people."
Thinking thus, at the end of the night he left his dwelling and, singing the name of Hari, went to Benapol.
There, in the midst of a dense forest, he sang sankirtana, and the people of the village came to worship him.
That greatly fortunate one to whom Krishna is merciful — every being who sees him is filled with devotion.
Seeing the radiance emanating from the body of Brahma Haridasa, gradually all the villagers became his devotees.
In that forest of Benapol the village devotees carefully built him a hut.
Living there, the sadhu served Tulasi and chanted ten million Names in a month.
He begged a handful of rice as alms in the houses of Vaishnava brahmanas; such is the nature of mercy: to teach the souls righteousness.
One day a prostitute, like a Vidyadhari in beauty, dressed herself up and came to Haridasa.
Sitting at the door of the hut, she began to display her body. Haridasa asked her kindly:
"Why have you come here in the evening?" The prostitute replied: "Seeing you, I have lost my head.
You have wondrous beauty and fresh youth: give up your sankirtana and enjoy pleasures."
Hearing this, Haridasa replied with a smile: "Go away from here today.
Whoever does not wear tulasi beads on the neck, whoever does not apply tilaka to the forehead,
on whose lips the name of Krishna does not appear — such people are contemptible unbelievers.
Know for certain: they have turned away from Krishna, and a sadhu never looks at their faces.
If you come in such a holy guise, then Krishna will fulfil your desire."
Having said this, the sadhu went on with his sankirtana, and the prostitute went home.
The next day she put tulasi beads round her neck and applied tilaka of gopichandana clay to her forehead.
Writing the names of Hari on her body, she dressed as a Vaishnavi and in the evening came to Haridasa.
Bowing to Vrinda (Tulasi), she sat at the door of the hut and for show loudly repeated: "Hari, Hari."
Boundless is the unearthly power of the company of saints: even by assuming a holy guise in pretence a soul obtains liberation in this life.
As an ordinary tree, standing beside sandalwood, absorbs its fragrance and itself becomes sandalwood.
Hearing the ceaseless name of Hari from the prostitute's lips, the crown of Vaishnavas praised her in the bliss of love.
Hearing the praise, the prostitute said to Haridasa: "Master, have mercy on me — for this I have come."
Hearing this, Haridasa said: "It is good that you have come. Say just once in a full voice: 'Hari, Hari.'"
Having said this, he began to sing the sankirtana of the Name, and listening to his singing the prostitute's heart was changed.
Through the shock of holy company she came to her senses and understood that the trade of a prostitute is nothing but the enjoyment of sin.
Bowing to Haridasa, she said with joined palms: "You are a great magnet-jewel: you have drawn me.
You are my master, my guru, a merciful wish-fulfilling tree. Take my side and grant me the fruit of liberation."
Hearing the prostitute's words, full of longing for dharma and firm faith, the crown of sadhus was immersed in the sweetness of love.
As atonement he shaved her head and, imparting power, gave the name of Hari into her ears.
Having received the name of Hari, she put forth a sprout of love, and Haridasa named her Krishnadasi.
The sadhu said: "Live here and chant the name of Hari: by the power of Krishna's mercy the desire of your heart will be fulfilled.
Brahman as the Name has the same power as the Supreme Brahman: through the Name one attains Krishna, and through a semblance of the Name — liberation."
Having said this, Haridasa went to another place, and Krishnadasi chanted the name of Krishna day and night.
Astonishing is the inconceivable power of a sadhu's mercy: a poisonous tree bears fruits of unearthly nectar.
Now hear of a wondrous pastime of Haridasa: how he made many yavanas servants of Krishna.
All the Vaishnavas living in the village of Phuliya were immersed in bliss on seeing Haridasa.
Gathering together, they ceaselessly sang the sankirtana of the Name, and it was as if a spear pierced the hearts of the unbelievers.
The governor of the yavanas, learning about Haridasa, in great anger said to his servants:
"In Phuliya there is a man named Haridasa: himself a yavana, he does the things of Hindus.
People laugh at him, and little by little the faith of the yavanas will perish.
Therefore seize him, bring him here and punish him." Receiving the command, the wicked servants ran off.
Seizing Haridasa and treating him with violence, they brought him to court with his hands bound.
Seeing Haridasa, the governor of the yavanas said: "Why do you, being of high caste, behave like a Hindu?
Whoever abandons his own religion and devotes himself to a great work (of another faith) will surely go to hell after death.
If you have in your mind the desire to reach paradise, recite the kalima and atone for your sin."
Hearing this, Haridasa replied in a deep voice: "I call that scripture best which is founded on reason.
Whoever follows a scripture consistent with reason is the best in all classes — so say the shastras.
The scripture of the yavanas contradicts reason: whoever follows it shows himself a yavana.
Here is the proof: the cow is mother and father, and an argument for killing the cow contradicts reason.
To eat its flesh is the same as eating one's father's flesh; yet their scripture prescribes killing the cow.
The births of these impious people multiply: by the fruits of their deeds they wander through various species of life.
The Supreme Brahman is the very being of all, the beginningless form (vigraha), full of the six opulences, with a body of pure goodness.
Scriptures that call Him formless and inactive — by reading them the delusion of maya grows.
In essence there is no difference between God and the soul — as the nature of fire is one in all lamps,
and yet the original fire remains chief; so Hari is the Lord of all and the support of all.
If one worships Hari, the soul's maya vanishes; with this aspiration I have taken shelter at the feet of Hari."
Hearing from the sadhu's lips proofs consistent with reason, all considered him a pir (a saint).
At that time the sadhu displayed his power, and the mlecchas, seeing it, were terrified.
Taking a straw between his teeth, the governor of the yavanas said: "O sadhu, be merciful to me, a lowly one.
I am ignorant and wicked: not recognizing you, I have committed an offence. Forgive me.
To your feet my millions of obeisances. By your goodness deliver me now, insignificant as I am."
Hearing this, Haridasa was moved to mercy and blessed him: "May your mind turn to Krishna."
Raising his arms, he said: "Say 'Hari, Hari': breaking the bonds of karma, you will obtain the boat of devotion."
Hearing this, all were filled with devotion and, crying "Hari, Hari," broke into dance.
Thus Haridasa delivered the yavanas and from there came to the town of Kuliya.
Boundless is the glory of Brahma Haridasa: even the gods do not know it — what then of insignificant me?
Through association with him Gosani Raghunatha Dasa obtained the seed of devotion and faith in Chaitanya.
He by whose mercy a serpent attained liberation in this life — what wonder if he delivered the yavanas?
Now I shall briefly tell of the deliverance of the serpent: hearing it, one comes to know the glory of a Vaishnava.
Haridasa sat in a cave chanting the name of Hari; hearing it, all the villagers came to him.
Seeing the sadhu's love and his taste for the Name, all began to sing the sankirtana of the Name with him every day.
At that time an enormous black serpent appeared: on its head a divine jewel blazed like the sun.
It stopped before Haridasa, coiled itself up and listened to the name of Hari.
Seeing this, all trembled with fear and said: "Best of sadhus, today you will lose your life."
Then the sadhu fearlessly took the serpent by the neck and, imparting his power to it, gave it the name of Hari.
Clapping his hands, he sang the name of Hari, and the serpent, hearing it, danced round in love.
Tears flowed ceaselessly from both its eyes; again and again it bowed its head to the Vaishnava's feet.
Receiving the dust of the Vaishnava's feet and hearing Brahman as the name of Hari,
the serpent before their eyes obtained a perfect body and, becoming four-armed, departed for the divine Vrindavana.
All the people, seeing this inconceivable glory, became Vaishnavas and devoted themselves to the name of Hari.
After some days a longing seized the sadhu, and he appeared in holy Shantipura.
Sri Advaita Prabhu, seeing His beloved Haridasa, said, "Come, father!" and floated on the waves of the bliss of love.
Seeing Shripada Prabhu, Brahma Haridasa prostrated himself with the eight limbs of his body and spoke humbly.
The Lord embraced him and said sweet words: "Give up your humility — I consider you equal to My own life."
In talk of the Beloved both were immersed in love and, crying "Hari!", raised their arms and broke into dance.
Thus day by day the festival grew. The high-caste brahmanas said among themselves:
"If the Acharya does not give up His association with Haridasa, He must certainly be excluded from the community."
The Acharya paid no attention to this, and the unbelievers excluded the Lord.
The Lord said: "Good, good — bad company is gone: Bhagavan has shown Me mercy."
Hear a wondrous account: in Shantipura there lived a rich high-caste brahmana.
Invited to an auspicious ceremony at his house, more than a hundred brahmanas came in great delight.
Having been honoured, all took their seats. At that time a certain sannyasi came there.
His form shone like the sun; by the radiance of his body all the directions were lit up.
He sat under a tree and did not utter a word; all the people came and bowed to him.
All the blind, the dumb and the others who came to the sadhu smeared their whole bodies with the dust of his lotus feet.
By the touch of the dust of the sadhu's feet their ailments went away, and all of them in great joy broke into dance.
The blind received sight, the lame received feet, the dumb spoke — their misfortunes passed.
Seeing this wonder, all the high-caste brahmanas, proud of their learning, and the unbelievers
came and bowed at the sadhu's feet, tying cloths round their necks, and offered him praises of many kinds.
For the sake of serving the sadhu they humbled themselves greatly. The sadhu said: "I eat nothing but the prasada of Vishnu.
The prasada of Vishnu is supremely holy; food not offered to Vishnu is like filth.
The gods, the ancestors and the saints accept nothing but what has been offered to Vishnu.
Whoever disregards this eternal word of the shruti will surely fall into a terrible hell."
The host of the ceremony said: "In my house there is Narayana; I shall offer you His prasada."
Saying "So be it," the sadhu agreed, and then they seated him in the assembly of brahmanas.
Like the moon amid the host of constellations, so the best of sadhus shone amid the assembly of brahmanas.
They carefully served the sadhu his food, and then began to serve it to the brahmanas.
When the feeding of the brahmanas was over, the Lord came there.
The all-knowing Sri Advaita, the guru of the world, is a wish-fulfilling tree for the pure devotees.
Seeing Brahma Haridasa in the assembly of brahmanas, the Lord smiled slightly and said gently:
"Dear Haridasa, what have you done? You have deprived so many brahmanas of their caste!"
Haridasa replied: "Lord, it was not my will: I sat down at the special insistence of the brahmanas."
Having said this, he quickly rinsed his mouth, bowed to the Lord and offered Him many praises.
Seeing this, the brahmanas were amazed and said: "The Acharya is Vishnu Himself come down to earth.
That Haridasa, for association with whom we excluded Him, is full of unearthly virtues.
The body of a devotee of Hari is perfectly pure: to see caste in him is a great sin.
We have offended the feet of Sri Advaita, and He out of mercy has taught us through His devotee."
Having said this, the brahmanas joined both palms, tied cloths round their necks and came to the Acharya.
Then the Lord out of mercy revealed His true form: Maha-Vishnu and Sadashiva — two in one form.
Seeing that form, the brahmanas were filled with ecstatic emotion: tears, trembling, the hair on their bodies standing up like kadamba flowers.
They said: "Lord, we take shelter at Your feet. Forgive our offence and place Your holy feet on our heads."
Prostrating themselves with the eight limbs of their bodies, they offered praise, and all drank the water that had washed the Lord's feet.
The Lord said: "Brahmanas, do not be afraid: the name of Hari has inconceivable great power.
Chant this Brahman as the Name and sing sankirtana — and the desires of all will be fulfilled without difficulty."
Having said this, Sri Advaita went home, and the brahmanas by great good fortune became Vaishnavas.
Boundless is the glory of the feet of a Sri Vaishnava: insignificant I do not know even a drop of it.
If, when good fortune dawns, a mleccha obtains devotion to Krishna, he obtains brahmanhood — so sing the Vedas.
As bronze becomes gold by a certain elixir, so by the path of devotion pure goodness is born.
The brahmanas had a base nature — by the power of a Vaishnava it was purified.
To reveal to the ignorant the glory of a Vaishnava, the Lord, passing over the brahmanas, gave the memorial dish (shraddha-patra) to Haridasa.
Haridasa, joining his palms, said to the Lord: "Why, instead of giving it to a brahmana, have You given the dish to me?"
The Lord replied: "A Sri Vaishnava has unearthly power: if you eat, it is the fruit of feeding ten million brahmanas."
Haridasa said: "You are the Sri Vaishnava-acharya: Your command must be accepted as scripture of dharma."
Hearing the name "Sri Vaishnava-acharya," the best of lords, overwhelmed with love, gave a loud roar.
In the company of Haridasa His jubilation grew; He constantly delighted in the kirtana of the name of Hari.
One day Haridasa said to the Lord: "The wicked mlecchas are destroying the eternal dharma.
They smash the Deities (murtis) of the gods to pieces and ruin everything needed for the worship of the gods.
The Srimad Bhagavatam and the other scriptures of dharma they seize by force and throw into the fire.
They take away the conches and bells of the brahmanas and forcibly lick off the tilaka and marks from their bodies.
They urinate on Sri Tulasi like dogs; in the temples they defecate like madmen.
Thus by hundreds of wicked deeds they contemptuously destroy every dharma and righteous act.
The firm vow of Krishna, known from the shastras: 'Whenever there is a decline of true dharma,
whenever adharma rises up — at every such time Krishna manifests Himself.'
Now that time has come. Why then has Krishnachandra not appeared?
How will dharma be protected, Lord? Thinking of this, I am constantly anxious."
The Lord replied: "Such is the way of this age of Kali: without the appearance of Krishna there is no remedy.
Bringing Krishna to appear, I shall spread the Name far and wide and deliver the whole world without difficulty."
Having said this, He roared loudly again and again, and Haridasa danced in the ecstasy of love.
Although Advaitachandra knows the whole truth, still He made a vow, following the custom of the world.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.
